analyst_view.overall: This is a relegation six-pointer before the international break. Hamburg are 15th after two straight league defeats and have only four open-play goals this season. Gladbach are bottom but unbeaten in three, with their first clean sheet in a 0-0 at Paderborn. Gladbach coach Alexander Blessin was reported unwell this week, and his side are missing several attackers.

goals.text: The numbers say 2.6 goals. Hamburg's attack has been toothless (only Schalke have fewer open-play goals), and Fabio Vieira is still out. Gladbach are without Nicolas Kühn, Hugo Bolin and Tim Kleindienst. With so much at stake at the bottom, a cagey game looks likelier than an open one.

corners.text: The numbers say 9.8 corners. Polzin expects an evenly matched game against a pressing Gladbach side, and nothing in the team news points clearly to more or fewer corners.

cards.text: The numbers say 4.0 cards. This is a scrap between 15th and 18th: Blessin wants a 'hungry' team, and Polzin's side could drop into the bottom three with a loss. Gladbach's aggressive pressing also tends to produce fouls, so we lean slightly higher.

shots.text: The numbers say 28.7 shots. Gladbach have lost their main forward options in Kühn, Bolin and Kleindienst (Kleindienst only returns after the break), and Hamburg have struggled to create in open play. Poulsen, Capaldo and Bornauw were all doubtful.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 10.2 shots on target. With Hamburg's weak finishing and Gladbach missing their best attackers, we expect fewer efforts to test either goalkeeper. Gladbach are also without their first-choice keeper, Moritz Nicolas, which may tempt Hamburg to shoot from range.
